A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PerceptionLM work, including complete Appendices A–M and references. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–53 are identical; page 1 differs only in author contribution symbols and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data scaling experiments, PLM benchmark evaluations and data ablations in Section 4.2 and Tables 3–6, with additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original scaling experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations and appendix quantitative and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The PE–Llama architecture, MLP projector, three training stages and data-generation procedures are identical in Sections 3–5 and the corresponding appendices.

E1.justification: Training data mixes and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including image/video benchmarks, PLM-FGQA, PLM-STC and all five PLM-VideoBench tasks. Appendices A and C–J introduce no coverage differences.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 3–5 and 11–15, including proprietary models, open-access VLMs, grounding specialists and human performance comparisons.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, data splits, sampling, preprocessing, metrics and evaluation procedures match throughout Section 6 and Appendices A, C, E and G–I.

E4.justification: The data-component ablations in Table 6, scaling analyses in Section 4.2 and Appendix B, and qualitative examples in Appendix K are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting and estimation procedures are identical. v3 adds or revises no run/seed information, uncertainty estimates, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted trends and qualitative outputs match. For example, Table 5 reports PLM-8B FGQA MBAcc of 67.7 and RTLoc meanR of 59.1 in both versions; appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The power-law formulation in Section 4.2 and mathematical definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about reproducible PLM training without proprietary distillation, synthetic-data limitations, 2.8M human annotations and PLM-VideoBench.

C2.justification: Interpretations of synthetic-data scaling and human-annotation benefits are unchanged. Appendix L retains the same limitations concerning long-video modeling, base-LLM dependence, SGQA performance and restricted data coverage.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, data recipes, annotation pipelines, inference/judge prompts and stated resource access information are identical. The updated arXiv version link does not change reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the complete reference list are identical. No cited works, novelty statements or positioning relative to prior research change.

P1.justification: v3 corrects first-page contribution notation: joint first authors receive asterisks, while project leads retain stars with a matching legend. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, axes, legends and placements are unchanged, including appendix displays. The page layout is retained; first-page differences are confined to contribution symbols and version/date text.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the first-page author contribution symbols, but the scientific exposition, methods, evidence, limitations and reproducibility information remain identical. This isolated editorial correction does not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
